title: CVE-2026-92392: HTTP/2 upload Use-After-Free
excerpt:
## Summary:
During a file upload, curl mishandles HTTP/2 RST_STREAM received from the server (with reason HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED or REFUSED_STREAM) leading to a use after free of a `struct Curl_easy` object. The control flow is a bit complicated, so I've produced an ASCII tree of the control flow to highlight the object lifetime issue in the Appendix below.

Preconditions for this are `curl -T <file>`, where `<file>` contains anywhere "<word> <word> <any>\n\n" and exceeds ~135KB. Our PoC exploit also requires `-Z`/`--parallel` when PIE/ASLR is enabled, but this is not necessary to trigger the memory corruption, only for exploitation.

As for how the UAF happens, after receiving the reset, multi.c converts the reset into a retry and calls `multi_done()`. In `multi_done()`, it calls `Curl_conn_ev_data_done()` which makes curl forget about the transfer, then it calls `Curl_req_done()`. Then `Curl_req_done()` flushes the buffered unsent remainder of the upload body into the connection. Since curl no longer knows about the transfer, it treats those bytes as a new request.  If they look like a request line, `h2_submit()` opens a new stream that stores a pointer to the `Curl_easy` object. This is the pointer that will be UAFed. After the retry completes, the application frees the `Curl_easy` object, but the connection still holds the pointer. It is dereferenced when the server sends a frame on that stream which can happen at exit, when the connection pool is destroyed.

## Affected version
8.22.0

## Steps To Reproduce:
I've attached a malicious server that triggers the bug (`evil-server.py`)

```bash
wget 'https://curl.se/download/curl-8.22.0.tar.gz'
sha1sum curl-8.22.0.tar.gz # should be 284e444b67f676a281906cfc86e9672780555cd4
tar xf curl-8.22.0.tar.gz
mkdir build ; cd build
# build with ASAN enabled
CC=clang CFLAGS="-O2 -g -fsanitize=address"" LDFLAGS="-Wl,-rpath,/opt/curl-release/lib" \
    ../curl-8.22.0/configure --prefix=/opt/curl-release \
      --enable-static --enable-shared --disable-docs --disable-manual \
      --with-openssl --with-zlib --with-brotli --with-zstd --with-libidn2 \
      --with-nghttp2 --with-libpsl --with-libssh2 --with-gssapi \
      --enable-ldap --enable-ldaps --enable-websockets --enable-mqtt --enable-ipfs \
      --enable-ntlm --enable-smb --enable-httpsig --enable-httpsrr --enable-ssls-export \
    && make -j"$(nproc)"
# make an examp

summary: curl mishandles HTTP/2 RST_STREAM with reason HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED or REFUSED_STREAM during a file upload, causing a use-after-free of a Curl_easy object that can lead to remote code execution.

claims.text: curl mishandles HTTP/2 RST_STREAM received from the server (with reason HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED or REFUSED_STREAM) leading to a use after free of a struct Curl_easy object
claims.reasoning: The code confirms the control flow: on RST_STREAM error, transfer.c skips Curl_req_abort_sending(), leaving unsent upload data in req.sendbuf. multi_done() then calls Curl_conn_ev_data_done() (which removes the stream from HTTP/2 filter) before Curl_req_done() (which flushes the buffer). The flushed data is parsed as a new HTTP request, h2_submit() creates a new stream storing the Curl_easy* pointer. When the transfer completes, data is freed but the connection pool retains the stream with the dangling pointer, causing UAF on later ingress processing.

Curl_req_done() called with premature=FALSE, so it flushes req.sendbuf via req_flush()
Curl_req_done() calls req_flush(data) when !aborted (aborted is FALSE here)
Curl_req_abort_sending() exists but is skipped on error path (goto out at line 272) when CURLE_HTTP2_STREAM occurs, leaving req.sendbuf unemptied
h2_submit() passes 'data' (Curl_easy*) to nghttp2_submit_request(), storing pointer in new stream when stream==NULL (treated as new request)

claims.reasoning: The UAF is a memory corruption (read of freed struct Curl_easy). While RCE exploitability depends on heap layout/ASLR, the vulnerability class (use-after-free) is a security issue per standard definitions. The project policy's 'NULL dereferences and crashes' exclusion does not cover controlled UAF from attacker-triggered server behavior during legitimate upload.

reply: Thank you for the detailed report and control-flow analysis. The code confirms the use-after-free: multi_done() clears the HTTP/2 stream (via Curl_conn_ev_data_done) before flushing the request buffer (via Curl_req_done), causing leftover upload bytes to be parsed as a new request that stores a pointer to the Curl_easy object. That pointer becomes dangling when the transfer is cleaned up, and is later dereferenced during connection pool shutdown. The fix should ensure Curl_req_abort_sending() is called on the retry path, or reorder multi_done() to flush before clearing the stream. We will investigate and apply a patch.
